pageCache.pageTitle: 2S Are Math Superstars! - News Blog - St Mary's Special School & College
pageCache.text:
2S Are Math Superstars!
These are pictures showing the children working on consolidating their understanding of the numbers 0 – 5. They had to pick a board, recognise the number, and then roll out that many balls of dough and put them in the 5-frame. They also had to try and find a loose, matching numeral. They all did well with this and are starting to realise that if a 5-frame is full, they don’t need to count the amount, they can just say, ‘5!’

pageCache.pageTitle: Medication - St Mary's Special School & College
pageCache.text:
Medication
Any prescribed or non-prescribed medication you would like us to give your child will need to be provided by yourselves and clearly labelled.
All medicines supplied must be sent in their original pharmacy supplied container and have a clearly legible pharmacy label with your child’s name and include;
• Medicine name (as it appears on the label)
• Strength (e.g. 125mg in 5mls)
• Form (e.g. capsules, oral suspension)
• Dose (amount to be given, e.g. one tablet, 5mg, and 10mls)
• Time (s) to be administered
• Route (e.g. mouth, gastrostomy, peg)
We ask that parents/carers check that the medicine has not passed its expiry date, as we cannot administer any out of date medication. Further liquid medicines must be in an unopened bottle or have the date of opening recorded on it. The Principal has the right to refuse to allow the school to administer medication. Please click on the link or scan the QR code to complete the medication administration consent form for your child.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parent/Carer Engagement and Reporting - St Mary's Special School & College
pageCache.text:
Parent/Carer Engagement and Reporting
At St Mary’s School and College we value parents and carers as essential partners in the education of our pupils/students. It is therefore important that we keep parents and carers appraised of their child’s progress throughout the year as well as their learning goals and ensure there is opportunity for Parental/Carer engagement throughout the academic year.
We do this through a series of meetings, and reports at regular intervals during the course of the year. Please see schedule below:
This event offers an opportunity for Parents/Carers early in the academic year to meet their child’s new teacher, staff team (including Therapy team) and see the classroom.
Pupil/Student Progress Report
A report containing your child’s progress towards their individual end of year target in the core subjects. The targets are generated based on prior attainment and their baseline assessment at the start of the academic year. All targets are individually set for each child in each subject allowing for appropriate challenge for them in each of their subjects.
Parent/Carer Consultation evenings
An opportunity to meet with your child teachers and therapy staff team to discuss your child’s progress as per their progress report received in term 2. Teachers will provide feedback on your child's academic performance, including their strengths and any areas in which they may need extra help.
Pupil/Student Progress Report
A report containing your child’s progress towards their individual end of year target in the core subjects. The targets are generated based on prior attainment and their baseline assessment at the start of the academic year. All targets are individually set for each child in each subject allowing for appropriate challenge for them in each of their subjects
This event offers an opportunity for Parents/Carers to see their child’s work have an informal discussion with your child’s teaching and therapy team and address any concerns rising from the Progress Report sent in Term 4.
Annual End of Year School Report
This will be a more detailed annual school report that reports on progress and achievement made throughout the academic year.
Please note in addition to the above your child will have an annual review, you will receive a detailed education and therapy report following this meeting. The date of this review will vary for each child depending on when their EHCP was issued.

Disability Support
The ability to communicate is fundamental to a basic quality of life, yet for many people effective communication is difficult because of a physical impairment, language disorder or learning disability. We work with people of all ages who face such challenges.
The general philosophy of autism Sussex is to provide a safe base for people with autistic spectrum conditions, where their special needs are recognised and from which they may take full advantage of community opportunities.
BILD is the British Institute of Learning Disabilities. Founded in 1971, we celebrated our 40th birthday last year.
Care for the Carers is an independent charity which supports unpaid carers in East Sussex who look after a relative.
Contact a Family is the only national charity that exists to support the families of disabled children whatever their condition or disability.
Disability Rights UK
We are disabled people leading change, working to create a society where everyone with lived experience of disability or health conditions can participate equally as full citizens.
Downs Syndrome Association
Providing information and support on ALL aspects of living with Down's syndrome to ALL who need it.
We exist to improve the lives of everyone affected by epilepsy.
Makaton is a language programme using signs and symbols to help people to communicate. It is designed to support spoken language and the signs and symbols are used with speech, in spoken word order.
Mencap is the leading voice of learning disability. Everything we do is about valuing and supporting people with a learning disability, and their families and carers.
We work with disabled people and their families. We offer practical support – from information services to education and everyday care.
The National Autistic Society
We are the leading UK charity for people with autism (including Asperger syndrome) and their families. We provide information, support and pioneering services, and campaign for a better world for people with autism.
Unique is a source of information and support to families and individuals affected by any rare chromosome disorder and to the professionals who work with them.

Ofsted is the Office for Standards in Education, Children’s Services and Skills. We report directly to Parliament and we are independent and impartial.

We provide children and young people’s mental health services across Sussex and Hampshire. Referrals to the service must be made my a parent/carer or professional working with the child to the East Sussex Single Point of Advice (SPoA)

Dragonflies offers free support to children aged 0-18 years old and their families who are experiencing pre or post bereavement. To make a referral please complete the Dragonflies Referral Form

A free service that offers workshops, discussion groups, resources and a weekly. Parents and carers can self-refer.

A team of public health practitioners, led by school nurses, who work with children, young people and families in East Sussex.
Single Point of Advice (SPoA)
Advises practitioners and other professionals with concerns about immediate risks to a child or young person, or any concerns reaching Level 3 or 4 on the Continuum of Need. For out of hours queries, contact the Emergency Duty Service.
Sussex Community Rail Partnership
Support for children and young people to travel independently by train, particularly those facing additional challenges such as special educational needs or disabilities.
Sussex Prisoners' Families
Support and advice for children, young people and families who have a relative in prison. Also offers training for professionals on awareness of related issues.
Sussex Recovery College
Offers educational courses about mental health and recovery which are designed to increase knowledge and skills and promote self-management.

pageCache.text:
School Meals
Children can choose to have a nutritious hot or cold school meal. We are committed to healthy eating and all residential pupils/students receive school meals, which are included in the fee. Day pupils/students are charged separately for a school meals. St Mary's does not use nuts in school meals.
Packed Lunch
If you decide to give your child a packed lunch, please choose healthy options. The packed lunch should not include sweets, fizzy drinks or drinks in glass containers.
